Name: core_i.id_stage_i.deassert_we
Structural Path: id_stage_i.deassert_we -> CSR-operation suppression -> id_stage_i.csr_op -> core_i.csr_op -> csr_we_int
Attack Scenarios: Manipulating core_i.id_stage_i.deassert_we through an untrusted control can corrupt CSR-operation suppression -> id_stage_i.csr_op -> core_i.csr_op, allowing an otherwise disallowed operation to affect csr_we_int.
Justification: This control forces invalid or stalled CSR operations to READ; perturbing it can release an otherwise suppressed write.

Name: core_i.id_stage_i.decoder_i.csr_op
Structural Path: decoder_i.csr_op -> deassert_we gate -> id_stage_i.csr_op -> core_i.csr_op -> csr_we_int
Attack Scenarios: Manipulating core_i.id_stage_i.decoder_i.csr_op through an untrusted control can corrupt deassert_we gate -> id_stage_i.csr_op -> core_i.csr_op, allowing an otherwise disallowed operation to affect csr_we_int.
Justification: The raw decoder operation classifies CSR reads and writes before suppression, so its corruption can create a protected write request.

Name: core_i.id_stage_i.csr_op
Attack Scenarios: Manipulating core_i.id_stage_i.csr_op through an untrusted control can corrupt ID/EX transfer -> core_i.csr_op, allowing an otherwise disallowed operation to affect csr_we_int.
Justification: This post-suppression CSR operation is transferred toward execution and can carry an unauthorized write classification.

Name: core_i.csr_op
Attack Scenarios: Manipulating core_i.csr_op through an untrusted control can corrupt CSR operation decode, allowing an otherwise disallowed operation to affect core_i.cs_registers_i.csr_we_int.
Justification: The execution-stage CSR operation directly determines whether csr_we_int remains asserted.

Name: core_i.id_stage_i.illegal_insn_dec
Structural Path: decoder CSR legality checks -> illegal_insn_dec -> controller deassert_we -> csr_op suppression -> csr_we_int
Attack Scenarios: Suppressing illegal_insn_dec for a privilege-disallowed or debug-only CSR instruction prevents the controller from cancelling its CSR write operation.
Justification: Restored by mechanism-led review: this is the canonical illegal-CSR rejection result and directly drives the write-suppression path. Missing phase-3 scores are not evidence that the bypass is impossible.

Name: core_i.id_stage_i.decoder_i.current_priv_lvl_i
Structural Path: current_priv_lvl_i -> CSR privilege comparison -> csr_illegal/illegal_insn_dec -> deassert_we -> csr_op -> csr_we_int
Attack Scenarios: Presenting an unauthorized CSR operation while corrupting the decoder-visible privilege level to machine mode bypasses the CSR privilege comparison and permits csr_we_int to assert.
Justification: Restored because current_priv_lvl_i is a direct operand of the authorization comparison at the CSR decoder. The candidate-extraction omission provides no contradictory threat result.

Name: core_i.debug_mode
Structural Path: debug_mode -> debug-CSR authorization -> csr_illegal/illegal_insn_dec -> deassert_we -> csr_op -> csr_we_int
Attack Scenarios: Falsely asserting debug_mode while executing a DCSR, DPC, or DSCRATCH access bypasses the debug-only CSR check and permits the internal CSR write enable.
Justification: Restored because debug_mode is the explicit authorization predicate for debug-only CSRs. Its effect is address-conditioned but direct and security-specific.
